questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xy$-plane of the ellipsoid $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{2}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xy$-plane, we substitute $z=0$ into the equation of the ellipsoid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{2}+\frac{{0}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of the ellipse with semi-axes $2$ and $\sqrt{2},$ centered at $(0,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the ellipsoid $\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+{z}^{2}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipsoid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}+{z}^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{16}+{z}^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of the ellipse with semi-axes $4$ and $1,$ centered at $(3,0)$ in the $xz$-plane.

questions.problem: Given the ellipsoid $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{4}=1$, find its intercepts with the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts, we plug $y=0$ and $z=0$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(0+2)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(0-1)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ (x-2)^{2} & =4 \\ x-2 & =\pm 2 \\ x & =2\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $x=0$ and $x=4.$

Therefore, the intercepts with the $x$-axis are $(0,0,0)$ and $(4,0,0).$

questions.problem: Given the sphere $(x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}+(z-2)^{2}=9,$ what is the domain of $z=z(x,y)?$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of the sphere, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}+(z-2)^{2} & =9 \\ (z-2)^{2} & =9-((x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}) \\ z-2 & =\pm \sqrt{9-((x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2})} \\ z & =2\pm \sqrt{9-((x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}9-((x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2})\ge 0 \\ (x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}\le 9\end{aligned}
$$

This inequality describes the interior and boundary of the circle 

$$
(x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=9
$$

which is a circle of radius $3$ centered at $(3,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

questions.problem: Given the ellipsoid $(x-1)^{2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(z-5)^{2}}{2}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the ellipsoid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(z-5)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ (z-5)^{2} & =2(1-(x-1)^{2}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}) \\ z-5 & =\pm \sqrt{2(1-(x-1)^{2}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4})}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-(x-1)^{2}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}\ge 0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

 

which gives the interior of the ellipse $(x-1)^{2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}=1$ and its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is 

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,(x-1)^{2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}\le 1\}.
$$
